faq.answer: No. Intensity may come from new closeness, unresolved conflict, caregiving, power, crisis, or attraction. The hypothesis needs repeated Type Two connection attention, matched comparisons, consent, and counterexamples.
faq.question: Does intense attention to one person establish this subtype?

faq.answer: Reciprocity shows whether standards apply when the helper needs support or when the other person says no. It makes hidden expectations observable without assuming that equal exchange is always required.
faq.question: Why test reciprocity in focused care?

faq.answer: Easy acceptance of limits, availability explained by explicit agreements, or stronger repeated attention to resources and group roles would weaken it. Attachment history and immediate safety should be checked first.
faq.question: What weakens the focused attunement hypothesis?

sections.body_md: The hypothesis combines Type Two needs-and-connection attention with a one-to-one label for concentration in one bond. Intense availability may instead reflect attachment, attraction, caregiving, conflict history, crisis, unequal labor, or a direct promise.
sections.title: Frame focused attunement provisionally

sections.body_md: This matched comparison asks about one bond and practical comfort by observing whether attention first moves toward focused connection, receiving care, or a useful role in the group. Keep the request, resources, and relationship risk comparable.
sections.title: Match one request across three priorities

sections.body_md: One-to-one is traditional organizing vocabulary, not evidence about bodily mechanisms, nervous-system categories, fixed intensity, or compatibility. A label never establishes consent, safety, attraction, or who should remain in a relationship.
sections.title: Protect consent and avoid mechanism claims

sections.body_md: Subtype traditions vary in how they describe attraction, pursuit, selectivity, and countertypical presentations. Test the specific focused-attunement proposition and let refusal, reciprocity, or calmer events revise it.
sections.title: Expect intensity descriptions to differ

sections.body_md: New intimacy, old conflict, caregiving duty, unequal responsibility, authority, boundary breaches, or immediate risk can concentrate attention on one person. Compare other bonds and safer periods before retaining the subtype.
sections.title: Test attachment, power, and crisis

sections.body_md: A one-to-one Type Two counterexample weakens focused attunement when limits are accepted easily, availability tracks explicit agreements, or matched situations repeatedly prioritize practical comfort and group contribution over one bond.
sections.title: Use reciprocal limits as a challenge

sections.body_md: Instrument-specific subtype evidence does not justify conclusions about compatibility, attraction, consent, or relationship quality. Direct communication, autonomy, safety, and environmental explanations take priority.
sections.title: Keep relationship inference narrow

sections.body_md:
Duration: 4

Context: Choose one close bond with consent to reflect, plus comparable practical and group requests that involve similar time and responsibility.

Observable signal: Record whose need receives urgency, how availability is negotiated, whether limits are accepted, and what reciprocity is requested directly.

Page-specific signal: Compare focused attunement with practical comfort and group usefulness while keeping the underlying request similar.

Alternative explanation: Test attachment, attraction, caregiving duty, unequal labor, conflict history, power, boundary breaches, and crisis against the subtype.

Reflection prompt: Identify the event where explicit agreement explains availability better than focused attunement and state how the hypothesis changes.

seo.description: One-to-one Type Two is a traditional type-by-instinct hypothesis in which Two attention to needs and connection may become concentrated in one bond through focused attunement, availability, and involvement. Two focused attunement is observable, but it does not establish attraction, consent, compatibility, or a universal subtype.
seo.title: One-to-one Type Two: focused attunement as a traditional hypothesis
